Two half-cells are set up as follows:

Half-Cell A: Strip of Cu(s) in $CuNO_3(aq)$

Half-Cell B: Strip of Zn(s) in $Zn(NO_3)_2(aq)$

When the cells are connected according to the following diagram, the following reaction occurs. What will happen in the salt bridge as the reaction progresses?
raw_record.standard_answer: The Na+ ions will flow to the Cu/Cu+ half-cell

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the left half-cell as Cu/Cu+ and the right half-cell as Zn/Zn2+, joined by a NaBr salt bridge. Use the net reaction shown: Cu+ is consumed in the Cu half-cell while Zn2+ is produced in the Zn half-cell. As Cu+ is reduced to Cu(s), the left solution loses cations and would become too negative relative to its nitrate ions. Therefore cations from the NaBr bridge must enter the Cu/Cu+ half-cell; specifically Na+ flows toward the Cu side. Br- would flow the opposite way toward the Zn side.
